findings.title: Anonymous private-room toggles trigger identical global room-list broadcasts
findings.prerequisites: One anonymous guest WebSocket; a private waiting room owned by that guest. No invite from another player, account, or privileged access required.
findings.reproduction: Create a private room; alternate {type:"ready",ready:true} and {type:"ready",ready:false}, allowing 120ms between messages; observe rooms messages on an unrelated client.
findings.impact: Each toggle within the existing control budget invalidates, rebuilds and broadcasts the entire public lobby snapshot to every socket, including players in private matches. Amplification scales with connected clients and public room-list size. Availability degradation at production scale was not measured.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep the last globally published encoded snapshot and suppress broadcasts when the public room list and online count are unchanged; continue answering explicit list requests. Avoid scheduling discovery updates for private-only state changes. Consider bounded per-source/control-churn rate limits without adding global connection/room admission ceilings.

hardeningSuggestions.classification: defense in depth; no authenticated WebSocket state exists
hardeningSuggestions.title: WebSocket upgrades accept arbitrary browser Origin
hardeningSuggestions.observed: Origin https://attacker.invalid completed /ws upgrade, received welcome and created its own anonymous room.
hardeningSuggestions.impact: A malicious webpage can create guest connections and exercise anonymous room/broadcast paths through visitors. This does not hijack an existing connection, reveal a private invite, or use account credentials.
hardeningSuggestions.recommendedFix: Reject browser Origin values outside an explicit set of canonical and intended alias origins before handleUpgrade; parse and compare complete origins including scheme and port. Keep an intentional policy for clients without Origin to preserve tooling.

additionalGameIntegrityReview.scope: Client-declared wins -> online match config -> combo/super gates only. Isolated loopback, two new anonymous peers, memory DB, provider:null.

results.description: create accepts unearned wins and only clamps the number
select can replace the count without changing fighter or winning a match
The authoritative start payload carries declared wins directly into PlayerConfig
Actual online execution grants the advanced combo to the forged-count guest and only the base combo to the zero-win peer
Shared authoritative engine gates super on declared wins, while independently enforcing 75 energy
results.note: Controlled pure-engine copies of server-issued start state; energy=100 was assigned only in these isolated local copies, never supplied over WebSocket or written to live server state.

verdict.confirmed: A guest can self-declare 9999 wins through create/join/select and unlock advanced combo eligibility and the super win prerequisite without any prior victory.
verdict.classification: Known trust boundary of anonymous local progression; real casual-match integrity limitation. No account/resource authorization barrier is crossed and no verified/global ranking exists.
verdict.impact: Advanced combo bonus becomes 7 instead of base 3 for the same light/light/heavy inputs. Super eligibility changes from locked to available once authoritative energy is at least 75; normal energy, cooldown, input and match-membership rules still apply. More than 3 declared wins does not further increase damage or add further unlocks.

designEvidence.meaning: Unlocks at 1 and 3 wins; super costs 75 energy
Progress explicitly localStorage; no global ranking or verified identity
Client reads wins from local storage
Client forwards local wins in selection
cleanWins normalizes and bounds; it does not verify history
Super trusts config.wins >=3 plus authoritative energy

verdict.recommendation: Keep existing offline/localStorage progression and open guest access. Describe online progress as client-declared and casual, and do not use this field for verified achievements, rankings, prizes or access authorization. If competitive parity is later required, add separate symmetric online unlock rules or an opt-in server-tracked/signed progression mode; retain existing local progression as unverified legacy progress without deleting or pretending it can be retroactively proven.

limits: Two anonymous loopback clients and small deterministic engine copies only; no account, DB persistence, paid generation, load test or other surface reviewed.
The actual online advanced combo was observed. Super eligibility/energy isolation was verified in shared-engine copies of the server-issued state, not by forging server energy over the network.
